# Abstract

The goal of this project was to build an end-to-end computer vision pipeline for detecting camouflaged, small, and partially obsured shark teeth. A high quality custom dataset was collected, an AWS Rekognition Custom Labels model was iteratively trained and improved, and a Flask + Render + PostgreSQL (or SQLite) website was created to serve as the front end. Extreme care was taken to ensure secret keys, access keys, and user information were never comprimised using environment variables, encryption, and modern authentication schemes. The model was measured to have an F1 score of 0.884, precision of 0.934, and recall of 0.840.

## Introduction

Hunting for shark teeth in places where they can be found in abundance is still a very difficult task. Shark teeth are often small, camouflaged, partially obscured, broken, and surrounded by rocks and pebbles of similar size and color. On a first expedition, one would be considered particularly talented or lucky if they were to find more than a couple of teeth in an entire day. While it is extremely challenging, with enough practice, some individuals are able to quickly and consistantly spot teeth, meaning that it is theoretically possible to train a computer vision neural network to identify and locate them in the sand.

![One Tooth in Each Picture](/assets/SharkTeethAssets/TeethHiddenInSieve.jpg)

## Problem Statement

Object detection for small or partially obscured objects is a notoriously difficult problem in computer vision. This project will provide a solution to the specific domain of identifying shark teeth where they can be naturally found. 

# Project Requirements

- Cross Platform Access
    - The model should be available anywhere and from any device. A mobile device or any laptop should be able to use the model effectively as long as there is internet access.
- Real World Performance
    - The model should out perform an inexperianced shark tooth hunter.
- Security
    - Access to the model should be limited to authorized personnel only.
        - Access and Secret keys should remain hidden at all points of the project, including development.
    - User passwords should be fully encrypted.
- Users
    - Personnel should be authenticated before they can be allowed to use the model.
- Availability
    - Anyone should be able to pull the code and be able to use their own resources to run everything.
